brief.recommendation: Memory veto (MEM-1) confirms terminating batch_replayable_price_sync was previously ineffective (checkout remained at 29% success). Waiting would cost ~$106,618 in lost revenue (596s remaining at $10,733/min per BIZ-4) and EXCEEDS the 60s degradation tolerance (BIZ-3). The workload is BATCH_REPLAYABLE with may_interrupt policy (BIZ-2), but termination is vetoed. No protected settlements in flight (DB-2). Escalation to the pricing team (workload owner) is the only viable path.

audit.report: A batch job (batch_replayable_price_sync, pid 108991) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4 seconds, blocking a checkout session and causing 4 timeouts. Checkout success dropped to 42% over 30 seconds with $10,733/min revenue at risk, far exceeding the 60-second degradation tolerance. The Database Guardian proposed escalation because a prior memory (MEM-1) verified that terminating this job was ineffective (checkout stayed at 29% success). The Continuity Guardian accepted, noting waiting would cost ~$106,618 in lost revenue. The incident was escalated to the pricing team after 51.3 seconds with no automated action taken.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction batch job (batch_replayable_price_sync) held a lock that blocked checkout sessions, and terminating it was historically verified as ineffective for recovery.
lessons: Add a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for batch_replayable_price_sync to prevent it from holding locks idle and blocking checkout.
Pre-stage a verified recovery runbook for batch_replayable_price_sync that includes lock-clearing steps beyond termination, since termination alone was proven ineffective (MEM-1).
Instrument batch_replayable_price_sync to emit lock-acquisition heartbeats so the detector can correlate lock holders with checkout degradation faster than 51 seconds.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly invoked the memory veto (MEM-1) and did not waste a round re-proposing termination; the Continuity Guardian accepted immediately with a clear cost-of-wait calculation. No guardian missed evidence or was overridden by an invariant.
follow_ups: Pricing team to confirm whether batch_replayable_price_sync can run with a shorter transaction scope or explicit lock timeout.
Verify that the 2-minute replay cost (policy may_interrupt) is still accurate and does not itself cause catalog inconsistency.
Update the workload registry with the verified ineffective-termination finding so future guardians see it without probing memory.
